                                     PROJECT NO. 58000
 RULEMAKING TO UPDATE                            §      PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
 WHOLESALE AND IOU RETAIL                        §
 TRANSMISSION COST RECOVERY                      §                    OF TEXAS
 IN THE ERCOT REGION                             §

    TEXAS RETAIL ELECTRIC PROVIDER COALITION’S COMMENTS ON THE
             PROPOSAL FOR PUBLICATION OF AMENDMENTS
                  TO §25.192 AND §25.193 AND NEW §25.252

       The Texas Retail Electric Provider Coalition (Texas REP Coalition) files these Comments

on the above-captioned Proposal for Publication (PFP) of Amendments to § 25.192 relating to

Transmission Rates for Export from the Electric Reliability Council of Texas (ERCOT), § 25.193

relating to Distribution Service Provider Transmission Cost Recovery Factors (TCRF), and new

§ 25.252 relating to Large Load Customer Tariffs.

       The Texas REP Coalition looks forward to working with the Public Utility Commission of

Texas (Commission or PUC), ERCOT, and all market participants on implementation of changes

to the manner in which transmission costs are allocated throughout the market and ultimately to

retail end-use customers. The rulemaking changes proposed here are a critical element of the plan

to integrate large loads in Texas without burdening the existing customers with the cost of

infrastructure that is sized to serve that load. One of the tenets throughout the ratemaking process

is to ensure that rates are reflective of cost causation to avoid cross-subsidization among customer

classes and to ensure that customer behavior that leads to lower cost of investment can be incented.

       These comments are offered from the perspective of understanding the timing challenges

and steps required to implement any cost allocation changes such that they flow through to end-

use customers as intended.
                                                                                            Page 2 of 5


                          I.     SYNCHRONIZATION OF TIMING

       It is important to factor in the time required to implement the proposed changes in order

for end-use customers to see an actual impact on the rates they pay for transmission cost. The

transmission cost allocation policy and the implementation of that policy should be set in a way to

synchronize the increased cost with the alteration of the cost allocation methodologies and

associated rate changes to the maximum extent possible.

       If the numerator of transmission cost revenue requirements to be allocated is increased, the

associated increase in the denominator of and methodology for total load to which that cost is

allocated should also be increased at the same time if the impact on rates of that aggregate cost

increase is to be offset by growth in the billing determinants. Otherwise, it is difficult to imagine

how the resulting rates could result in a scenario where residential and small commercial customers

do not experience material increases in transmission cost due to the construction of transmission

that is not necessary to serve those customers absent interventionist ex-post facto cost allocation

policies that would inevitably prove contentious and have many unintended consequences.

       The minimum demand charge for allocation of transmission costs is an ex ante approach

intended to align the cost allocation for upgrades resulting from the large load integration process

at ERCOT to those same large loads, and is a reasonable conceptual mechanism for aligning

recovery of those costs with cost causation. Under the rule as proposed, the transmission cost

allocation would only apply to large loads that meet the definition in 25.194 (a definition that has

not yet been adopted). While the Commission will receive extensive feedback regarding ways to

improve upon the minimum billing demand approach, the underlying principle is sound on a going-

forward basis: large loads are the planning input that results in the transmission upgrades and

associated costs and thus should pay their fair share of those costs, e.g., through something like
                                                                                                      Page 3 of 5


the minimum billing demand mechanism. This approach should be designed in a manner such that

transmission costs associated both with project-specific transmission build out and with

transmission associated with large load projections that are not project-specific are both assigned

fairly and paid by the customers in the rate class that were part of the underlying planning

assumptions that support the need for the projects.

                  II.      END-USE CUSTOMER RATE IMPLEMENTATION

        Current retail rate change mechanisms that are designed to minimize regulatory lag in rate

recovery for transmission providers rely on a look back of cost allocation methodologies. 1 This is

also true of the Unified Tracker Mechanisms. There will be no prior rate case class cost allocators

that are based on 12CP. It is unclear from the language what cost allocator is intended to be used

in determining TCRF calculations in between the time the rule is adopted and the utility’s next

base rate case. It would not be congruent to change the retail rate allocation methodologies until

the wholesale cost allocation methodologies are implemented.

        As an additional consideration in the timing, changes to the retail rate allocation

methodologies require a change to the systems at ERCOT that track customer CP demand. Those

systems are embedded in Texas SET.                Conversion from a 4CP methodology to a 12CP

methodology for retail cost allocation will require a change to Texas SET at ERCOT. Historically,

those changes take a period of months to years to implement. The Texas REP Coalition stands

ready to work with ERCOT to try to streamline and expedite the changes to Texas SET that would

be required to implement the new allocation methodology approved by the Commission.

        The issue of timing for rate implementation also comes with a risk that transmission costs

associated with large loads could be proposed for inclusion in rates before the load itself is


        1
           16 Tex. Admin. Code § 25.193(c), TCRF Formula, ALLOC is the class allocator approved in the last rate
case unless otherwise approved.
                                                                                             Page 4 of 5


energized or required to pay a minimum demand charge. The Commission should consider

approving a mechanism where the ongoing increases in transmission costs should be held as a

regulatory asset and not included in rates until such time as a mechanism is in place for the

Commission to require that these increased transmission costs are allocated to the large loads.

Also, costs for transmission projects that are sized based on anticipated large load demand should

not be charged to customers until those projects are energized and in service. Regardless of when

the cost allocation changes approved in this rulemaking are implemented in a manner that changes

the TDU charges to the retail electric providers, the rule should include language that makes clear

that the TDU must provide a minimum of 45-days notice to the retail electric providers after PUC

approval to allow for an appropriate implementation of those rates for inclusion in invoicing to

end-use customer charges. The Texas REP Coalition requests inclusion of the following language

in this rulemaking:

       The electric utility shall provide notice to retail electric providers of rates approved
       under implementation of this rule not later than the 45th day before the date the
       rates take effect.


                                     III.     CONCLUSION

       The Texas REP Coalition respectfully submits the foregoing comments, commits to

working with the Commission, ERCOT, and other stakeholders on ensuring a smooth end-use

customer-friendly implementation of the policy decisions made by the Commission, and requests

the Commission’s consideration of the issues raised as it adopts a final version of new § 25.192,

§ 25.193, and §25.252.

RULEMAKING TO UPDATE                           §      PUBLIC UTILITY COMMISSION
WHOLESALE AND IOU RETAIL                       §
TRANSMISSION COST RECOVERY                     §                   OF TEXAS
IN THE ERCOT REGION                            §
               TEXAS REP COALITION’S EXECUTIVE SUMMARY

    The cost of new transmission investment that is in whole or in part designed to serve
     projected large loads should be subject to the new cost allocation methodologies approved
     as a result of this project.

    The implementation of the proposed 12CP methodology, or any change to the current 4CP
     cost allocation will require a change to Texas SET at ERCOT.

    ERCOT’s required timing to implement that Texas SET change should be considered in
     deciding when to begin cost recovery through rates for the transmission investments that
     are planned to serve projected large loads.

    The rule should include language requiring the electric utility to provide notice to retail
     electric providers of rates approved under implementation of this rule not later than the
     45th day before the date the rates take effect.
